### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

Examples, using `search_method = 'cover'`:

- If I use a treesitter text object, e.g.
    ```lua
    custom_textobjects = { c = ai.gen_spec.treesitter { a = "@class.outer", i = "@class.inner" } }
    ```
    If I'm inside the class and use `vac`, I would like it to select the class regardless of how large the class is. Right now, `mini.ai` says "no match" if the class is bigger than `n_lines`.

- If I do `van"` to select the next double-quoted string, I don't want it to select a string that's entirely outside the current window, though it's okay if the string is only partially shown.

These seem related, but not identical. The second point might be too ambitious with its partial coverage logic, but disabling the `n_lines` limit for `gen_spec.treesitter` objects seems like it could be doable.

comment_data.body:
> These seem related, but not identical. The second point might be too ambitious with its partial coverage logic, but disabling the `n_lines` limit for `gen_spec.treesitter` objects seems like it could be doable.

Only by adjusting the `config.n_lines` to be very big. This will have effect on all textobjects. So the options are:
- Use very large value globally, i.e. set in `require('mini.ai').setup()`.
- Set it in `vim.b.miniai_config` per buffer. Like if there is an attached tree-sitter parser.
- Have custom mapping that sets or toggles between different predetermined values. This would require extra step, but might be not so bad.

There is no plans of making `n_lines` dynamic to fit both use cases, I'm afraid. The only possible improvement might be to entirely remove this config altogether, but it comes at a performance cost. I did try to make it increase smartly like 1, 10, 100, etc., but it felt too complicated and unpredictable.

reply_data.bodyHTML:
Thanks, I figured the "only overlapping the visible window" logic might be a bit heavy.

Doing this seems to work to allow selecting huge class definitions without globally setting a huge n_lines:

local ai = require('mini.ai')

local ts_class = ai.gen_spec.treesitter({ 
  a = "@class.outer", 
  i = "@class.inner" 
})

require('mini.ai').setup({
  custom_textobjects = {
    c = function(ai_type, id, opts)
      opts.n_lines = 99999 
      return ts_class(ai_type, id, opts)
    end
  }
})

reply_data.body:
> Thanks, I figured the "only overlapping the visible window" logic might be a bit heavy.
> 
> Doing this _seems_ to work to allow selecting huge class definitions without globally setting a huge `n_lines`:

Oh, yeah, I forgot about the return value of the `gen_spec.treesitter` and that it can be used as a callable. I'd only made sure that `opts` is not `nil` in this custom wrapper. Other than that, it does indeed seem to do the job! Nice!
